dave_customer: Hey team — customer reported 502 / TLS handshake failures from their app to our private VPC endpoint. Only happens when egress goes through their corporate proxy. Works from a laptop on mobile network.

alice_support: thanks, can you paste the client logs and any s_client output?

dave_customer: pasted minimal repro:
```
# from a pod behind their proxy
openssl s_client -connect private-api.redwood.internal:443 -servername private-api.redwood.internal -tls1_3 -msg
CONNECTED(00000003)
139763...:error:1425F102:SSL routines:ssl_choose_client_version:unsupported protocol:ssl/statem/statem_lib.c:2000:
139763...:Alert: Handshake Failure (40)
---
Protocol  : TLSv1.2
Cipher    : 0000
---
```

alice_support: OK that's interesting — s_client fell back to TLS1.2 and then failed. Do you have the proxy product/version?

dave_customer: They're using "SecureGate GW v8.1" (appliance) and their infra team says they only allow a restricted cipher list and RSA key exchange.

bob_infra: Quick hypothesis: our endpoint presents an ECDSA leaf cert (or prefers ECDHE suites) and the proxy doesn't advertise compatible curves/ciphers, so the proxy terminates TLS to upstream and fails to negotiate. Can you get the proxy TLS logs showing ClientHello -> ServerHello?

carol_enterprise: from the proxy logs I see: "ClientHello: versions [TLS1.2 TLS1.1], ciphers: RSA+AES256-SHA RSA+AES128-SHA". No ECDHE entries and no TLS1.3. Upstream handshake attempt -> "no shared cipher".

alice_support: that's consistent. Our served cert chain is ECDSA leaf (signed by our/private CA) and we prefer ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256 in TLS1.2 and full TLS1.3 suites. If the proxy removes ECDHE and ECDSA support, they'll have no overlapping suites.

ssl-bot: Suggestion: show mutual supported cipher sets. Run on your proxy box: `openssl s_client -connect private-api.redwood.internal:443 -servername private-api.redwood.internal -cipher 'RSA' -tls1_2` and `-cipher 'ECDHE'` to compare.

alice_support: Also please confirm if the proxy does TLS interception (terminates and re-initiates) or is a pass-through (SNI passthrough). If it terminates, it must be configured to accept ECDHE/ECDSA or to allow passthrough to upstream.

dave_customer: They confirmed it is a terminating proxy doing TLS MITM for inspection. Ops says their policy enforces RSA-only ciphers for compliance.

bob_infra: Two safe remediation paths: (1) update proxy TLS profile to allow ECDHE and modern curves (recommended), or (2) on our side offer an RSA-signed certificate alternative or a compatible cipher-suite fallback for that customer's dedicated endpoint. Which is viable?

carol_enterprise: Ops won't allow ECDHE due to their old HSM limitations. They asked if we can serve an RSA leaf or enable TLS1.2 RSA-ECDH fallback.

alice_support: We can provision a compat RSA-cert variant for Dedicated/Private customers but it requires a cert rotation and might reduce forward secrecy. Need Product sign-off for security tradeoff.

bob_infra: Quick temporary workaround: can we tell the customer to switch their proxy to TLS passthrough for traffic to private-api.redwood.internal (SNI allowlist)? That avoids MITM and preserves ECDHE/TLS1.3.

carol_enterprise: They can add an allowlist entry for SNI, but their security team is resistant. They asked for a strict list of ciphers/versions to open. Can we provide a minimal compatible set that keeps reasonable security?

alice_support: Yes — if they at least enable TLS1.2 and ECDHE suites with curves secp256r1 and secp384r1, acceptable minimal ciphers: `ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256`, `ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256`, and TLS1.3 default suites. That preserves PFS and modern AEAD.

ssl-bot: For appliances that cannot do ECDSA, enabling `ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256` plus `TLS1.2` is a pragmatic compromise. Note: TLS1.3 only negotiates its own suites and requires both sides to support TLS1.3.

dave_customer: Customer wants a clear repro for our internal SRE to test config changes. I ran curl through their proxy and captured the CONNECT flow:
```
> CONNECT private-api.redwood.internal:443 HTTP/1.1
< HTTP/1.1 200 Connection established
# then proxy tried TLS upstream and failed
< TLS handshake error: no shared cipher
```

alice_support: For our internal runbook: 1) Confirm proxy termination mode. 2) Collect proxy ClientHello (ciphers + curves). 3) Try SNI passthrough allowlist as test. 4) If passthrough not allowed, consider providing RSA-signed cert on customer's endpoint or request Product approval. 5) Share minimal cipher list to open.

bob_infra: I'll spin up an ephemeral test endpoint with an RSA cert to validate their proxy accepts RSA suites. Can you give me an IP/hostname I can put in their allowlist?

carol_enterprise: I'll ask Ops for a short maintenance window for an SNI passthrough test tomorrow 02:00 UTC. I'll also request ClientHello capture.

alice_support: Thanks. If you get captures, upload them (pcap or hex) and ping me. If we need to issue an RSA cert we can fast-track with Security but will log risk.

dave_customer: Confirmed — Ops scheduled a test window. I'll post the capture after the test. Thanks all :thumbsup:

alice_support: Noted. I'll prepare an internal PR describing RSA cert fallback steps and required approvals so SRE/Product can review.

bob_infra: Quick note for SRE: if you create RSA endpoint, don't forget to disable OCSP stapling mismatch and ensure chain is compatible with their proxy CA store. Some proxies drop ECDSA chains if they don't trust the chain signature algorithm.

carol_enterprise: got it — will include CA fingerprints in allowlist request.

ssl-bot: If you need an immediate diagnostic, run `openssl s_client -connect private-api.redwood.internal:443 -servername private-api.redwood.internal -curves secp256r1,secp384r1 -cipher 'ECDHE' -tls1_2` and `-cipher 'RSA' -tls1_2` and paste outputs.

alice_support: leaving this thread open until the capture/test completes. Appreciate the quick coordination.

(edited)
